content: This document provides a summary of information about the medication and does not include all possible details. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete guidance regarding this medication and your individual health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Azasite Uses: This medication is prescribed to treat specific bacterial eye infections. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for other types of eye infections. How to Use: Before using this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Wash your hands thoroughly before applying the eye drops. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication or if you have an active bacterial eye infection. Before each use, shake the dropper once while holding it upside down, then remove the cap. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and place one drop into the pouch. Look downward and close your eyes gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eye. If you are using other eye medications (such as drops or ointments), wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying the next medication. Use this medication regularly at the same time(s) each day to achieve the best results. Continue using it for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve. Side Effects: Temporary eye irritation, stinging, burning, or blurred vision may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to other types of eye infections, including fungal infections. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using azithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin or clarithromycin), ketolide antibiotics (such as telithromycin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred. Use caution when performing activities that require clear vision. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if azithromycin passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone swallows this medication and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store unopened bottles in the refrigerator. Once opened, the bottle can be stored in the refrigerator or at room temperature. The medication expires 14 days after opening. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. Discard any unused medication after completing treatment or after 14 days. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete and personalized information about this medication and your specific health needs.
